speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the detailed history. The relief of symptoms with voiding and dyspareunia are significant clues. Given the chronic nature and exclusion of infection, have you noticed any pelvic pressure or a sensation of a lump in your vagina?

Also, have you had any prior urinary tract infections or pelvic surgeries?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The pain during intercourse (dyspareunia) combined with your relief from voiding is highly suggestive of bladder pain syndrome. To confirm if there is bladder wall inflammation, I am requesting a CT cystogram or MRI. Do you have any history of interstitial cystitis, and have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle that might relate to your pelvic symptoms?
